points: The next earnings report could show FY2026 organic growth tracking at the high single-digit guidance after FY2025's 10.1%; that would mean the slowdown is orderly, not a collapse, and support the long case.
The same print will reveal whether the $80M Project Empower savings are lifting adjusted EBITDA margin; if margin stays close to the 31.7% FY2025 level, the bear case on profitability weakens.

Delegated Authority revenue, which doubled to $1.4B and reached 47% of sales in FY2025, could keep growing faster than the 10% YoY falsifier; that would confirm the shift toward a higher-margin, scalable business.
If diluted EPS recovers from the $0.47 FY2025 level, the 57.7x P/E could compress through earnings growth rather than a falling stock price, which is the main long payoff.

Peer reports from GSHD on Oct 22 and AJG on Nov 5 will set the tone for insurance brokers; strong E&S pricing commentary would back RYAN's pricing-power tailwind, while weak prints would pressure the high multiple.
Over the next 12-18 months, further acquisition integration could add revenue and cost synergies on top of the $80M program, helping offset the FY2026 organic-growth moderation to high single digits.
If the next print shows adjusted EBITDA margin falling below 28% or EPS sliding toward the $0.40 falsifier, the long thesis breaks because the 396 P/E would be exposed to a sharp drop in valuation.
The theme is warm and leaning short, so a clean RYAN quarter could trigger relative outperformance as shorts cover and investors rotate to the broker with the strongest operational momentum.
